text: You're down six points.
why: Precise state at a glance; no narrativizing.

text: Your aide tells you the votes aren't there yet.
why: Fact delivered fast through a familiar person; summarized dialogue fits the moment.

text: The bill fails, 47–52.
why: Minor event at minor weight; exact count preserved.

text: Your brother pays back the money you lent him.
why: Ordinary continuity referencing a prior choice without melodrama.

text: Your mom calls. Your uncle died this morning.
why: Grounded directness for a serious event; no cinematic suspense.

text: Your mom looks over the bills again. 'Not this month.'
why: Restricts itself to what the child observes; asserts no household-finance knowledge.

text: Life in Kentucky carries on much as before.
why: Valid transition treatment; deletion (NO PROSE) is equally valid.

text: You've been at it for three hours. Most people aren't home.
condition: campaign texture / narrative setup
why: Natural campaign register without insider jargon.

text: A woman near the food stand recognizes you before you can introduce yourself.
condition: setup for a quick interaction or dialogue that actually follows
why: Grounded public-recognition setup.

text: I know who you are.
condition: only if the encounter actually proceeds into dialogue
why: Direct dialogue earns its place when the exchange is played.

text: Your phone lights up with Jordan's name. You haven't spoken in four years.
condition: the four-year gap is canonical
why: Strong old-relationship setup grounded in established history.

text: The new poll has you six points lower than last week.
condition: summarized/scene information surface
why: Same fact as status UI, rendered for a narrative surface.

text: Your campaign manager slides the new poll across the table. You're down six.
condition: an actual campaign-office scene is being played
why: Scene staging supported by packet facts.

text: For once, there's nowhere you have to be. The weather is perfect.
condition: 'for once' requires canonical prior busyness; weather established
why: Relaxed free-day narration; ordinary life allowed to be ordinary.

text: If you want it, you can start Saturday.
why: Direct-dialogue job offer; casual voice fits the speaker and moment.

text: The manager offers you a weekend job starting Saturday.
condition: setting up a player response
why: Summarized form of the same offer when the exchange itself needn't be played.

text: You keep your voice down.
condition: the player explicitly chose to remain calm
why: Observable action; choice outranks trait; no internal-conflict narration.

text: You surprise yourself by staying calm.
condition: very strong established trait plus the player's explicit choice; use sparingly
why: Limited interpretation earned by strong evidence; never automatic.

text: Months of work end on a 47–52 vote.
condition: months of work are canonical
why: Weight earned from canonical importance, not engine traceability.

text: Marcus has backed you before. Now he's asking you to vote yes.
condition: prior support is canonical AND especially relevant to this decision
why: Continuity referenced only when it earns its place; natural familiar reference.

text: By the afternoon, everyone seems to be talking about it.
condition: a major established development with a plausible ambient information path
why: World reaches the character plausibly without interrupting the scene.

text: Vote no.
why: Action label describes the action; expectations exposed separately via grounded context.

text: Sure. Go eat with them.
condition: casual moment
why: Casual wording for a casual action; no bureaucratic register.

text: Your aide thinks leadership will take a no vote badly.
condition: the aide's expectation is established; paired with a plain 'Vote no.' choice
why: Likely-but-uncertain consequence exposed through a grounded channel, not baked into the button.

text:
HB 218
Second reading complete
Amendment pending
Floor vote tomorrow
why: Telegraphic institutional UI; political specificity preserved.

text: HB 218 cleared its second reading. An amendment is still pending, and the floor vote is tomorrow.
why: Same facts as the UI form, rendered as narrative summary.

text: Harris leans toward the microphone and offers an amendment to your bill.
condition: Harris is established; use 'Representative Harris' when effectively unknown
why: Familiarity controls reference form; institutional action stays specific.

text: You read the motion again before the hearing.
why: Second person held even though the packet's CHARACTER line names a judicial role.

text: HB 214 comes up Thursday.
condition: the player is the bill's sponsor
why: Designation kept exact; authorship the player already knows is not restated.

text: She's offering you $500 for your time.
why: Money stated as an actual arrangement rather than a UI label.

text: $500 to play two songs.
condition: the terms are established in the packet
why: Terse money phrasing that still names what is paid for; not an abstract offer label.

text: People here are not going to vote for a library tax.
condition: ordinary conversation where 'tax' is factually accurate
why: Natural spoken term preferred over the stiffer 'library levy'; formal filings may keep the legal term.

text: How do you respond?
condition: the scene has reached its decision pressure
why: Explicit, owner-preferred return of control; the scene stops as soon as the player can act.
